definition: A named technique ('Blocking Plus') for the extra blocking pass a shot needs before spline: rather than just adding generically more poses, deliberately stagger DIFFERENT BODY PARTS to different timing and contrast within the same pass — favoring one arm's pose to hold longer then arrive quicker, planting a leg sooner than the rest of the body so there is somewhere for the hips to shift weight into later — so 'not everything has to move all at once at one speed in one direction all stopping on the same frame'. The blunt numeric framing: a 200-frame shot blocked with only 20 keys hands the computer 90% of the shot's decisions the moment spline is hit.
purpose: Give a concrete, per-body-part METHOD for the 'add more keys before spline' principle, rather than leaving 'more keys' as a vague quantity — specifically, stagger which part leads/holds/arrives when, using body-mechanics reasoning (where does the weight need to go, what has to plant first to receive it) rather than adding keys uniformly across every control.
visible_effect: Different body parts visibly move at different times and speeds even within one continuous blocked action — one part held static while another moves, one part overshooting while another eases — rather than the whole body moving in lockstep and stopping together.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Named directly as what makes a character 'feel more alive, fluid, organic' versus mechanical — the SAME contrast-in-timing idea existing corpus entries already cover for measured lead/lag, here framed as a deliberate BLOCKING-STAGE method rather than a post-hoc curve adjustment.
physical_interpretation: A real body's parts do not start and stop simultaneously — a foot plants before the hips can shift weight onto it, an arm's follow-through lags a shoulder's initiation — this technique authors that physical asymmetry directly into the blocked poses rather than relying on physics simulation or curve interpolation to introduce it later.
use_cases: any blocking pass on a shot with more than one moving body part, deciding per-part which one leads, which one holds, and which one arrives late, based on body-mechanics reasoning rather than uniform timing
specifically, planting a foot earlier than the rest of the body to create a base the hips can shift weight into on a later frame
non_use_cases: a shot or moment where genuinely simultaneous, uniform motion across all parts is the intended read (a rigid mechanical object, a specific stylistic choice for uniformity)
interactions: key_density_gates_spline_readiness_not_a_fixed_rule and spline_should_refine_not_fix_posing_defects (this same batch, video 95) — this entry is a THIRD independent confirmation of the same underlying principle (enough blocking-stage information before spline), with a specific, named method ('Blocking Plus') for what that extra information should actually contain, which neither of the video-95 entries state.

The existing corpus's chain lead/lag entries (W02) describe the MEASURABLE result of exactly this kind of staggering; this entry is the blocking-stage AUTHORING method for producing it deliberately, body-mechanics-first.

style_variations.semi-realistic: timing contrast follows real body-mechanics reasoning
style_variations.stylized/goofy: the same underlying contrast technique still applies, but the specific choices (what leads, what holds) can depart further from realistic reference — stated directly as still needing the same underlying skill, just aimed differently

cadence_representation: Not represented as a named technique, though the underlying capability exists: `ai/motion.js analyseChain` already measures lead/lag, and `authorMotion`'s breakdown/settle steps can already place per-joint keys at different pose fractions — nothing currently packages 'stagger these specific body parts for a body-mechanics reason' as a guided step the way `authorMotion`'s other phases are guided.
control_surface: Ordinary per-joint keyframe authoring (`set_keyframe`) with deliberately different timing per control; `authorMotion`'s breakdown/settle bias parameters, applied per-joint rather than uniformly.
detection_and_measurement_methods: `analyseChain`'s existing lead/lag measurement would show this staggering directly if present, and a near-zero lag across all parts of a blocked action (per the existing `rigid_unit_motion_flag` check, LESSONS.md #29) would be evidence this technique was NOT applied.
generation_or_modification_methods: Achievable today via per-joint keyframe authoring with deliberately different frame placements; no new capability required, only the body-mechanics judgment of WHICH part to stagger and why.
failure_modes: adding more keys uniformly across every control (more density but no staggering), which raises key count without adding the contrast that actually reads as organic
staggering parts arbitrarily rather than for a body-mechanics reason (setting up where weight needs to go), producing motion that is busier but not more purposeful
roblox_considerations: None specific — a pure blocking-stage authoring technique independent of the target engine.
examples: the presenter's own words, verbatim: 'this could be as simple as just favoring an arm pose to stay in one position longer and then arrive quicker later[,] or it could mean having a leg shift faster[,] planting a foot much sooner so that there's somewhere to actually shift all this weight in the hips later on' (transcript 6:03-6:16), and the numeric framing: 'if you have a 200 frame shot and you only had say 20 keys to begin with... the computer is now responsible for 90% of your shot' (transcript 2:46-2:57)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/KSRZg7PwgyU @ 2:24-2:57 and 5:24-6:22 — Sir Wade Neistadt names 'Blocking Plus' directly and demonstrates the per-body-part timing-contrast method with a worked backflip example, transcript-only per this video's detail setting; experimental until validated
